Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace contract, then inspect the inherited rollout evidence—including both moving-window visual views—before proposing or editing the single candidate. I’ll also consult the fish-control bookshelf at the required decision point and keep the transfer reasoning in the designated notes file.

The workspace requires two skill-guided checks here: the bookshelf transfer protocol for controller mechanisms, and the wake-visual protocol for interpreting both evaluation views. I’m applying both before any policy edit; the visual skill will determine what motion failure the candidate should address, while the bookshelf will constrain the mechanism to a transferable body-frame invariant.

The two sampled behaviors are both valid direct-uniform still-water captures, so the useful contrast is not success versus crash: it is the reproducible 19.31 T route versus the prefilled 18.99 T route. Both sheets show self-propulsion with a coherent alternating wake and no visible loss of wake organization near capture; the improved sheet closes slightly sooner along a very similar arc. I’m now isolating which policy change and trajectory/action metric explains that small semantic gain, so the new candidate tests a distinct mechanism rather than another scalar retune.

The evidence supports one mechanism-level extension. The current winner removes the posterior traveling-wave pose from proportional route geometry and gains 0.314 T, but its measured recent yaw remains strongly gait-correlated after the existing head-only rate correction: across 2 T to capture, a fit gives approximately `raw_yaw_rate ≈ route − 0.681·q̇1 − 0.162·q̇2`, while the policy compensates only `0.4·q̇1`. I’ll preserve the raw-geometry redirect and add a conservative whole-wave derivative common-mode only to ordinary route feedback. This is the bookshelf’s “separate rhythmic gait motion from slow target steering” invariant, expressed through observed joint rates—not a carrier gain retune.

The candidate and durable lesson are now updated. The policy change is deliberately narrow: ordinary route-rate feedback now sees the posterior traveling-wave derivative, while the evaluated carrier, pose projection, raw redirect logic, and actuator allocation remain unchanged. I’m moving through contract, symmetry, and schema checks now; no CFD will be run.

The first required checker found a rendered-workspace metadata defect: `README.md` marks the same parent optimizer as “prefill” twice, so the checker counts two markers even though there is only one assigned parent directory. The policy/guidance content has not failed yet. I’m inspecting the checker’s supported inputs and workspace metadata to resolve this without touching the frozen solver surface or weakening the semantic comparison.

All three prescribed checks now pass after repairing the duplicated parent marker in the rendered `README.md`: guidance provenance, lightweight Julia policy contract, and editable-boundary validation. I’m invoking the workspace’s dedicated check-runner now for the required independent no-CFD verification.

The dedicated checker role could not start because its configured `gpt-5.4-mini` model is unavailable on this account; that is an infrastructure error, not a policy failure. The prescribed commands already pass locally. I’ll still obtain the required independent check by assigning the same immutable TOML procedure to a standard validation agent, with no edits and no CFD.

Independent validation is complete: guidance provenance, Julia contract, editable boundary, and the deterministic schema audit all pass; all 58 referenced parameter fields are declared. The shadow comparison also confirms the intended isolation: when posterior tangent rate is zero the candidate is parent-identical, and when it is nonzero the ordinary route rate changes while the raw redirect request remains exactly unchanged. No CFD was run.

Produced exactly one candidate: `v31_whole_wave_pose_rate_projection`.

- [Candidate policy](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:12) adds whole-wave derivative rejection to ordinary route feedback while preserving the validated raw redirect behavior.
- [Wake-policy notes](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:3) contain the visual diagnosis, evidence, bookshelf transfer block, hypothesis, and falsification criteria.
- [Reusable guidance](guidance/control_experience.md:66) now incorporates the sampled whole-wave projection result and applicability boundary.
- Removed a duplicated assigned-parent marker from `README.md` that initially prevented the required provenance check.

All no-CFD checks pass: guidance provenance, Julia contract, editable boundary, non-empty candidate, and parameter schema (`58/58` references declared). Formal CFD remains for EvE.
